chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Qummi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

Say: O Allah, I ask You for conviction for myself, and forgiveness, and well-being in this world and the Hereafter. O Allah, You are my trust, and You are my hope, and You are my support, and You are my helper. With You I disembark and with You I travel.

He (peace be upon him) said: And whoever goes out on a journey alone, let him say: 'Whatever Allah wills, there is no strength except by Allah. O Allah, comfort my loneliness, and help me in my solitude, and complete my absence (from home).'
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications for a Muslim traveling alone?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on supplications in the road, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the Shia emphasis on integrating spiritual mindfulness with daily activities, particularly travel. It underscores the concept of *tawakkul* (reliance on Allah) by invoking Him as the ultimate source of strength and comfort, while also addressing the psychological aspect of solitude through specific invocations for those journeying alone. This practice reflects the broader tradition of transforming mundane actions into acts of worship through mindful remembrance (*dhikr*).
